findings.rule: The renderer replaces each blocked term in the store data it embeds with the term's label in square brackets, such as `[SESSION_MEMORY_URL]`.
findings.input: A store with a single ledger/s1.url whose URL contains a PUSH_BLOCKLIST term (e.g. PUSH_BLOCKLIST="x.test" and s1.url = "https://x.test/code/s1"), rendered with --format html or md and no --session-url
findings.finding: The session URL that storeUrl reads from the store's ledger/*.url file is passed unmasked to renderPage (embedded as session_url) and to renderMarkdown (used as the fallback link of every thread), so a blocked term in it reaches the page and the scan still fails.

findings.rule: A page rendered from a store whose events carry a blocked term passes the scan.
findings.input: PUSH_BLOCKLIST="term" (or any term that is a substring of a label, such as "BLOCK" or "MEMORY") with an event note "term"
findings.finding: maskTerms writes labels that can themselves contain a blocked term, and later replacements in the reduce rewrite inside earlier labels, so the masked page still contains the term ("[PUSH_BLOCKLIST term 1]" contains "term") and the label no longer stands intact where the term stood.
